tierNamesSource: rsssf.org/tablesf/fran02.html prints "Division 1" for 2001-02; fran03.html prints "Ligue 1 (NB: name change from Division 1 to Ligue 1)" for 2002-03
sourceNotes: Every page was fetched raw (curl) and parsed by script, never through a summariser, so printed names are exactly as each source prints them.

rsssf.org: franfullhist.html (France first division tables 1932 to 1998) for 1990-91 to 1996-97; season pages franYY.html for 1997-98 to 2008-09 and franYYYY.html (YYYY = end year) for 2009-10 to 2025-26.

LFP: ma-api.ligue1.fr (season = start year) returns tables from 1993-94 and nothing for 1990-91 to 1992-93; for those three the LFP's own historic standings page on lfp.fr, as archived by web.archive.org on 2007-11-24, is the league source.
ESPN (site.api.espn.com, season = start year) returns Ligue 1 tables from 2002-03 only; it is a third source on 2002-03 to 2025-26 and agrees on every one.

worldfootball.net could not be read (a Cloudflare challenge on direct fetch, HTTP 402 through WebFetch), and statscrew.com has no Ligue 1 tables (its l-FRA1 standings page is empty), so neither is used.

verified is true when the two primary sources (rsssf and the LFP) list the same clubs, and, where ESPN exists, ESPN lists them too. All 36 seasons meet that. Positions: pos is set when rsssf and the LFP print the same place; posPrinted lists every source's place wherever any source differs.
keyNote: key is this ledger's own identity for a club across sources and seasons, set by an exact alias table, never by a fuzzy match (AC Ajaccio and Gazelec Ajaccio stay two clubs, Paris FC is not PSG). canon is the Soccer Career spelling from HAND_CLUBS in src/lib/soccerCareerEngine.ts; only eight French clubs exist there (PSG, Marseille, Lyon, Lille, Monaco, Nantes, Strasbourg, Nice), so every other club is canon null.
